title: the Yoga Vasistha (selections)
hook: praise and insult pass through a free king like sounds
tomorrow: the long talk ends. what does Rama say he'll do now?

segments.voice: Yesterday, the Yoga Vasistha's young teacher Kumbha told the king: burn the hut, and the grip can still be there. Today, the grip is gone. Then what?
screen: `GIVE UP THE GRIP, NOT JUST THE THINGS.`

segments.voice: After the last exam, the last shift, the last day of a big project, there's a strange quiet. Now what? The king in Vasistha's story reaches a quiet like that. He has finally let go of the grip, the sense of mine and I, and something in him has gone still. He's free. And he's sitting in a forest hut with no kingdom, no wife and nothing to do. So, what does a free person do next?
screen: `THE LAST EXAM IS DONE.` → `A FREE KING IN A HUT.` → `NOW WHAT?`

segments.voice: Chudala doesn't reveal herself right away. In the story she tests him, more than once. She arranges an invitation to heaven, and he declines without fuss. She stages a betrayal in front of his eyes, and he isn't shaken. Praise and insult reach him the way sounds reach a still room: they arrive, they're heard, they pass, and nothing is left clinging. Then she lets the disguise fall. Kumbha, his teacher, was his wife all along. And his answer to the question, what next, isn't to stay in the forest. They go home. He takes up the kingdom again, and the two of them rule together. That's the surprise in the ending. Freedom here doesn't require a forest. The king had to go there to learn it, but he didn't have to stay. Hearing cases, eating, talking, ruling: all of it can be done by someone none of it grips. Vasistha tells this to Rama, a prince who will rule one day, and who came to court half ready to walk out of the world.
screen: `HEAVEN DECLINED. A BETRAYAL, UNSHAKEN.` · `THE DISGUISE FALLS.` · `HOME, TO RULE TOGETHER.` · then, large: `FREEDOM DOESN'T NEED A FOREST.`

segments.voice: Choose one sound around you: traffic, a fan, a bird, your own breath. Listen to it for the whole sit. Some moments it will be pleasant and some moments it will grate; let each one arrive, be heard and pass, without holding on to the nice ones or pushing the harsh ones away.
The Yoga Vasistha: here, a king unshaken by pleasure or insult, who goes home free and rules again.
Keep this one: the Yoga Vasistha, in selections, where the free king goes home. That's sixteen-oh-seven.

screen: `DAY 1607 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: WHAT WILL RAMA DO NOW?`
